items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: Another fellow, Buddy Collins. He was from here... He was a vocalist... But he got over it. We often laugh about that. If we hadn't stayed away a couple of days, old Nick Turner would have been buried over there in Ashland.

ctx.x: What about if a guy got sick? And you're on the road.

That's another question. It's hard for me to answer. I don't remember anybody getting sick, but one time was Turner, wasn't it? What about that? Well, that was in later years. But Henry Turner got real sick in a little town of Ashland, Kentucky, I think. It was in the hills. And we had to...no, I'm sorry. Another fellow, Buddy Collins. He was from here. I don't know if you ever hear any talk about him. He was a vocalist. You've told me about him. Yeah. Well, Nick Turner got sick in this little small town in the…
I don't know if he's still going or not. You were going to say something?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: We'd be cooking on his stove and I would share some of his vittles with him, talk about music and at regular procedure, how I'm doing and how you're doing and so forth and so on.

ctx.x: So you had a fairly good age even then. That's right. When you went over across the lake into Susquehanna, I think you wrote to Ropeman you went to Mandeville, and then Buddy had a place. In Covington.

To Covington. Right. In Covington. Buddy had an old shack way back in the woods. What would you all talk about? Well, just everything in general. We'd be cooking on his stove and I would share some of his vittles with him, talk about music and at regular procedure, how I'm doing and how you're doing and so forth and so on.
But would he explain to you anything about the trumpet or was it just in general? No, just in general. I didn't know if he gave you any sort of lessons or?
